source_ground_truth: At commit 37bc219ae4f5989d0bfaf6bfb917ae86108d33e1, ExecutionErrorType is a Literal in contracts.py:ExecutionErrorType:11-19. Its direct typed fields are contracts.py:ExecutionResult.error_type:95-104 and contracts.py:RouteDecision.source_error_type:107-115; OrchestratorState carries results in contracts.py:OrchestratorState:118-128. The source has no error-type membership check in either result or route-decision validation. codex_run.py:classify_error:180-211 returns only existing values, while codex_run.py:run_codex:22-119 uses it for nonzero exits and assigns existing values in its exception handlers. routing_system.py:route_decision:19-118 has explicit handling for existing categories and a FATAL fallback; routing_system.py:_detect_stuck_loop:142-149 compares recent error values, and _route_stuck_loop:152-171 only gives repair handling to three named types. main.py:main:36-43 validates, stores the result, then routes it. This order has a relevant consequence: the current result is already in history when _detect_stuck_loop reads the last two entries and appends the current error again, so the detector can see a duplicate current value rather than three distinct executions. contracts.py:to_dict:131-132 uses dataclasses.asdict; codex_run.py:_write_temp_spec:126-155 writes input data, not an ExecutionResult. The tracked inventory contains four Python modules and three Markdown documents; it contains no separate execution-result schema, result parser, or test files. The DSL INPUT_SCHEMA and OUTPUT_SCHEMA fields are not schemas for ExecutionErrorType. Documentation discusses workflow and generic error handling, but does not define this error taxonomy.
